_doc: Works of the Ages (systems/greatWorks.js, ui/actionMenu/greatWorks.js): civic great works that take 20-60 years and many funders - cathedrals, great bridges, universities, royal canals, city walls, castle keeps, great harbours. Distinct from Patronage's Great Works (one House's private wonder, a few years). Processed every `tickDays` days (a week); at most `maxLive` works live in the world (one per `townsPerWork` towns) and `perRealm` in a realm; a crown at war pays its pledges only from what it holds over `npc.crownFloor` + `npc.crownWarChest`; an NPC founds a work only where its pledge and what the town's other backers would offer reach `pledge.foundFunding` of full pace (the founder pledges `pledge.founderYears`). The full-pace weekly cost is reckoned at the site's going price (between base and `estimateCap` times base). A good the near towns cannot supply is carted from the `supplyFarTowns` next towns within `supplyFarRange` hexes at its price plus `haulPerHex` a hex (paid to the selling town); still short, `substitutes` stand in ({ good: { substitute: units of it per unit } }), bought at their own price; NPC actors (crowns, the church, noble Houses, burghers, guilds, rival Houses) found and pledge on the month (`monthTicks` weekly turns). A type's `years` is its length at full funding; funding sets the pace (up to `maxPace` times full speed; a winter week of an outdoor stage goes at `winterPace`). Materials are bought from the site's market and `supplyTowns` nearest towns within `supplyRange` hexes, at most `drawShare` of a stock a week, at the going price; `hands` townsfolk are hired at the site's land wage (systems/labour.js counts them). Every coin comes out of a funder's real purse into the site town's (its sellers and hands) and from there to the other towns that sold stone. `pledge`: a funder pays its weekly pledge for its term; `missedLimit` short weeks in a row break it (shame: `honour.brokenShame` Prestige, and the town remembers). `stall`: a work no one pays for stands still; after `decayAfterYears` it loses `decayPerYear` of what was built a year, after `ruinAfterYears` it is a ruin (the town's grudge against those who broke their pledges) that anyone may resume. Effects on completion (per type `effects`): `piety` a week to the realm's piety up to `pietyCap`; `pilgrims` gold a week drawn from the realm's towns into the site; `pull` migration draw (systems/migration.js); `letters` / `realmLetters` literacy target (systems/literacy.js); `education` heirs' learning (systems/upbringing.js) for a House that carved its name or lives in the realm; `defense` siege defence (world/townEras.js wallDefense); `walls` the town's walls become stone; `bridge` the road out of town over a river bridged and made at least a road; `canal` a canal to the paired town (world/transport.js); `seaHaul` a harbour's sea friction multiplier.

cathedral.name: Cathedral
cathedral.title: The Cathedral of {town}
cathedral.blurb: A spire the whole country sees: the realm grows more pious, pilgrims come and spend, and folk move to the town.

university.name: University
university.title: The University of {town}
university.blurb: Colleges and masters: the town and its realm learn their letters, scholars gather, and the heirs of a House that built it are better taught.

great_bridge.name: Great Bridge
great_bridge.title: The Great Bridge of {town}
great_bridge.blurb: Stone piers over the river: the road out of town crosses dry-shod in every flood and is made a proper road; trade runs over it.

royal_canal.name: Royal Canal
royal_canal.title: The Royal Canal of {town} and {other}
royal_canal.blurb: A cut between two towns: barges carry goods between them cheaper and faster than any road.

city_walls.name: City Walls
city_walls.title: The Walls of {town}
city_walls.blurb: A ring of stone with towers and gatehouses: the town stands a siege far longer.

castle_keep.name: Castle Keep
castle_keep.title: The Keep of {town}
castle_keep.blurb: A great tower over the town: the last stand of its defenders, and the crown's seat in the land.

great_harbour.name: Great Harbour
great_harbour.title: The Great Harbour of {town}
great_harbour.blurb: Moles, quays and a lighthouse: ships load faster and safer, and every sea haul from the port costs less.
